findings.title: Item-resume failures mark the original batch run as failed
findings.description: When item resume reuses the batch `run_id`, an exception from the resumed pipeline reaches `_run_pipeline`’s `except BaseException` handler, which finalizes that existing run as `FAILED` before re-raising. For example, a mid-item `GitEnvironmentError` is then reported as `HALTED`, but the original batch run’s status has already changed. This contradicts the item-resume contract that the batch run remains completed and can mislead callers inspecting run state.

findings.title: Malformed report item shapes escape the load-error contract
findings.description: `BatchReport.load` casts `report["items"]` to a list of dictionaries without validating either shape. If `items` is a string or contains a non-object entry, `BatchItemRecord.from_json` calls `.get()` on that value and raises `AttributeError`, which is not caught here. The CLI then gets an unexpected exception instead of the documented `BatchReportLoadError` and `REJECTED` result for a malformed report.

findings.title: Mutating fan-out pipelines can bypass the project run lock
findings.description: `_step_mutates` only traverses nested steps in a `steps` list, but fan-out stores its nested step under `inner`. The executor runs that inner step, and fan-out validation does not restrict it to non-mutating types; a mutating inner step can therefore be run without the lock. Concurrent invocations could then interleave git/Context Forge mutations despite the run-lock guarantee.
